item.title: Google DeepMind Prioritizes Lifelong Learning in Hiring
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: One of Google DeepMind's top execs says lifelong learners will have an edge in the AI workplace
Lila Ibrahim, Google DeepMind's chief AI readiness officer, emphasized that candidates with multiple credentials demonstrate a learning mindset. She stated that while degrees matter, recruiters prioritize résumés showing lifelong learning, curiosity, and the ability to ask good questions. These skills are critical in an AI-powered workplace, where knowing how to ask questions is becoming harder to teach. Ibrahim highlighted the need for interdisciplinary collaboration, citing examples like pairing philosophers with engineers to drive technical breakthroughs. Google DeepMind founder Demis Hassabis also stressed the importance of humanities alongside STEM fields. A study found that 75% of organizations have deployed AI, but only 18% reported widespread employee upskilling. Ibrahim noted increased diversity in UK talent compared to Silicon Valley, with stronger appreciation for philosophy and political science. AI is reshaping jobs rather than replacing them, requiring workers to develop both technical and human skills.

item.title: Bill Gates Warns of 20-Year AI Transition Turmoil
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Bill Gates predicts 20 years of turmoil before AI creates 'true abundance'
Bill Gates warns of a 20-year transition period marked by widespread job disruption before AI enables 'true abundance.' On the 'Decoder' podcast, he predicts white-collar roles like telesales, accounting, and support will be replaced by AI, while humanoid robots will take over blue-collar jobs. He envisions a future where AI handles most economic tasks, rendering human labor unnecessary for many goods and services. Gates emphasizes the need for measures like early retirement or work hour caps to preserve human employment, suggesting some may adopt a 'Amish-like' approach limiting AI use. He also highlights the importance of work for purpose and relationships. Other tech leaders like Elon Musk and Sam Altman have expressed similar concerns, though Altman notes fewer white-collar job losses than expected. Despite corporate layoffs, national unemployment remains stable during the AI boom.

item.title: Oceanside to Install Braces on Fire-Damaged Pier Ahead of Storms
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Braces to be installed on fire-damaged Oceanside pier to shield against El Niño storms
Temporary braces will be installed on the fire-damaged Oceanside Municipal Pier to stabilize it against El Niño storms and support future repairs. City Engineer Brian Thomas said the braces, part of a $428,982 contract awarded to Jilk Heavy Construction, will help maintain the damaged end of the pier through winter storms and during deck and railing replacements starting late next year. The project is funded by $3.38 million in insurance proceeds from the April 2024 fire that destroyed a restaurant and kiosk. The city council approved the contract after two bids exceeded the estimated cost. The fire, deemed accidental by federal investigators, damaged the pier’s hammerhead section, which remains closed. Permanent repairs, expected to take eight months, will follow. Insurance coverage includes up to 75% reimbursement for uncovered costs through Cal-OES. The pier, originally built in 1888, has undergone multiple rebuilds, with its current structure dating to 1986.

item.title: Parents Weigh Selling Home to Help Kids Buy Homes Now
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Should you give your kids their inheritance early?
Parents considering selling their home to help children buy homes now face risks like capital gains taxes, long-term care costs, and rising rent. Liz Weston, a certified financial planner, advises against cashing out assets, noting selling could trigger a 15%-20% federal capital gains tax and California income tax. Inheriting the home would avoid these taxes but delay the inheritance. Alternatives like downsizing or gifting portions of the home, which may require gift-tax returns but not actual tax liability, are suggested. Renting carries risks of increasing costs despite rent control. A fiduciary financial adviser and tax professional can help structure gifts efficiently. A separate letter discusses using overpayments to offset future taxes, though IRS delays may occur despite efforts to apply refunds to future years.

item.title: Saudi Arabia seeks U.S. AI aid to counter Yemen's Houthis
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Saudi Arabia looks to US for an AI edge as Yemen's Houthis up pressure
Saudi Arabia is seeking U.S. AI assistance to counter attacks from the Houthi group in Yemen. Despite U.S. President Donald Trump refusing direct military involvement, the U.S. is providing intelligence, including an AI targeting system similar to the Maven Smart System (MSS). MSS, developed under Project Maven, aggregates surveillance data to identify potential targets like rocket launchers or vehicles, speeding up the 'kill chain' for military strikes. U.S. personnel in Saudi Arabia help operate the system, which has been used in conflicts in Iran, Iraq, and Syria. However, MSS faces challenges in Yemen due to the Houthis' mobility and terrain, as well as ethical concerns over civilian casualties. Analysts note that while AI enhances targeting speed, it risks unintended harm, as seen in an Iranian school strike. Experts argue that AI may not defeat the Houthis, who have high tolerance for destruction and rely on tactics like mobile missile systems and drone swarms. The conflict remains unresolved despite ongoing military efforts.

item.title: AI agents help manage daily tasks but raise privacy concerns
item.description:
Source: Vox Original headline: When AI agents run your life
AI agents are gaining traction as tools to manage daily tasks, offering time-saving benefits but raising privacy concerns. Sari Azout, a tech worker and mother of three, found relief using Meta’s Muse to handle back-to-school logistics, describing the experience as transformative. Reece Rogers, a Wired reporter, explains agents as proactive digital assistants that integrate with emails, calendars, and other data to streamline tasks. Current tools include Meta’s free Muse and OpenAI’s paid Dots, with Muse connecting to Facebook Marketplace for shopping. Users report benefits like finding discounted items, but privacy risks loom as agents access sensitive data like bank accounts and personal details. Muse’s terms automatically use user interactions to train Meta’s AI, prompting warnings to disable data sharing. Rogers notes marketing efforts focus on cuteness, with mascots like Muse’s fluffy design aiming to build trust. Despite AI backlash, Rogers predicts widespread adoption, comparing it to ChatGPT’s rise. While some users gain leisure time, others caution against over-reliance and data exposure.

item.title: Ukraine Uses Drones as WiFi Repeaters to Extend Attack Range
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Ukraine is using drones like hovering WiFi repeaters to help attack drones reach farther
Ukraine is deploying drones as signal repeaters to extend the range of its attack drones and counter Russian jamming. Twist Robotics' Saker Scout drone, originally a reconnaissance platform, now serves as an airborne relay, boosting operational range by over 50 kilometers. Rostyslav Olenchyn, the company's co-founder, explained that existing drones lacked sufficient range for modern missions, prompting a redesign for signal relay. These drones, operating as flying WiFi repeaters, maintain stable connections over long distances and difficult terrain, resisting Russian electronic warfare tactics. Other Ukrainian firms like Roboneers and Skyriper are also developing similar technology. Ukrainian forces use these repeaters to maintain radio links with strike drones, enabling extended missions. Russia has adopted similar tactics to extend its drone reach. The US military is also exploring relay systems for drones, addressing the challenge of maintaining control and communication at tactical distances. Updates to drone capabilities, including signal repeaters, are critical in the evolving conflict, with new features released every two weeks.

item.title: Del Mar to hold pedestrian safety workshop
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego
Del Mar will host a pedestrian safety workshop next Thursday at 4:30 p.m. at the Civic Center Town Hall. The free event, co-hosted by the city and Del Mar Community Connections, will be led by California Highway Patrol Officer Jared Grieshaber and university researchers. The TREDWise workshop aims to train participants to recognize risk factors and remain alert to common pedestrian hazards. Grieshaber will emphasize traffic rules and defensive walking techniques to enhance street safety. The initiative is linked to the UC San Diego-based Transportation Research and Education for Driving Safety Center, which brings together experts in public health, medical engineering, law enforcement, and neuroscience. The center's mission is to prevent traffic-related injuries and deaths by promoting safer roadway behaviors. City officials highlighted the collaboration as part of efforts to improve safety in Del Mar's walkable downtown area.

item.title: Plushie Mimics Data Center Hum to Highlight Environmental Concerns
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: This sold-out plushie emits the grating hum of a real-life data center when you squeeze it
Bezzy, a gray plushie with a server-rack abdomen, emits the grating hum of a data center when squeezed. The sound is a recording from a Virginia data center. Artist Rajeev Basu, founder of Basura, described the process of selecting the sound as 'weird' and noted the hum is 'terrifying.' The plushie is part of a satirical art project called 'Adopt a Data Center,' which highlights concerns about data centers' environmental and community impacts. The project, created in collaboration with musician Alan Wilkis, includes stickers and bumper stickers with humorous messages about AI infrastructure. Basu emphasized the need for public education on data centers, which have sparked nationwide protests and some local bans. The 20 limited-edition Bezzy dolls, launched in September, are sold out. Market research shows rising plushie sales among younger generations, with millennials and Gen Z driving demand despite broader toy industry struggles.

item.title: Target shifts holiday strategy to shorter, faster updates
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Target is turning the holiday marathon into a series of sprints
Target is shifting its holiday strategy to shorter, faster updates as part of CEO Michael Fiddelke's turnaround effort. The retailer plans to reset US stores in the first week of November, followed by another overhaul in the first week of December after Black Friday. A new micro-season will focus on the final 10 days before Christmas, with stores transformed into 'Christmas Morning Magic' featuring fresh stocking stuffers priced from $3 to $20. Chief merchandising officer Cara Sylvester emphasized the change, noting the seasonal section will replace leftover items with new products. Target is adopting strategies from its revamped SoHo store, which uses early resets and flexible fixtures to maintain freshness throughout the season. Fiddelke highlighted the holiday season as a culmination of year-round efforts, stressing the need for a hectic yet organized approach. The strategy aims to address late-season momentum struggles faced by retailers, ensuring last-minute shoppers find available items.

item.title: Los Angeles Could See First Rainy Halloween in Over a Decade
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: More storms a-brewin': Could L.A. see its first rainy Halloween in over a decade?
Los Angeles could face its first rainy Halloween in over a decade as a storm system brings a 90% chance of rain between Friday and Nov. 2. Meteorologist Rich Thompson warned Halloween activities may be impacted, with moderate-level storm conditions likely. The last recorded rainfall on Halloween in LA was in 2014, when 0.25 inches fell. Before that, rain occurred in 2003 and 1987. Coastal flood advisories are in place due to historically high tides, with water levels expected to reach 7.5 to 8 feet above baseline in Los Angeles, Orange, and San Diego counties. Orange and San Diego coasts face localized flooding, erosion, and road closures. A coastal flood warning remains active through Thursday, urging residents to prepare for rising waters and potential property damage.

item.title: Vista's Bobier Elementary opens as all-electric school for 600 students
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Vista's rebuilt Bobier Elementary opens as all-electric 'campus of the future' for 600-plus students
Vista's Bobier Elementary School opened as an all-electric campus for over 600 students. The $100 million rebuild, funded by Measure LL, a 2018 voter-approved bond, includes three playgrounds, turf fields, a track, and modern classrooms. The school generates 90% of its energy through solar panels, making it financially efficient and sustainable. Principal Melanie Paliotti emphasized the diverse learning opportunities, including dance, music, visual arts, and STEM programs. Superintendent Matt Doyle described the campus as 'awe-inspiring,' designed to feel spacious and conducive to learning. Fifth grader Jerson Bacasehua expressed excitement about being part of the school's legacy. The project, completed in two years, aims to provide students with a comprehensive environment for education, play, and connection.

item.title: Caltrans, SANDAG to Resume Rail Work in Batiquitos Lagoon This Weekend
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego
Caltrans and San Diego Association of Governments will resume rail work in Batiquitos Lagoon this weekend. The project, delayed by weather, involves rail destressing and replacing an 80-year-old wooden trestle bridge with a modern steel-and-concrete structure. Work will occur Saturday night through Sunday morning, focusing on tracks south of La Costa Avenue overcrossing. The double-track project aims to enhance the LOSSAN rail corridor's reliability and capacity by adding a second track from Avenida Encinas to La Costa Avenue. The new bridge will widen lagoon channels, improving tidal and flood flows for wildlife. Public areas near the railroad right-of-way will experience construction noise, equipment sounds, and additional lighting for crew safety.

item.title: Over 400 San Diego Residents Without Power After Outages
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: More than 400 without power following outages across San Diego County
More than 400 residents in San Diego County are without power following outages. The affected areas include Vista, Rancho Bernardo/Rancho Penasquitos, and downtown, where power was lost since around 11:30 p.m. last night. SDGE reported three outages caused by damaged equipment. Restoration is expected by 5 p.m. today for downtown, with Rancho Bernardo’s outage set for 6 p.m. today. SDGE stated crews identified a transformer issue in downtown and are working on repairs. Some outages may have delayed restoration timelines while crews assess damage. Estimated restoration times are now updated on the ERT website.

item.title: Six Flags Adds Seat Belts to Some Rides After Georgia Death
item.description:
Source: Washington Post Original headline: Six Flags to add seat belts to some roller coasters after death in Georgia
Six Flags announced it will add seat belts to some roller coasters following the death of Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, who fell from the Goliath ride at its Georgia park on October 12. The company's CEO, John Reilly, stated the move includes Goliath and similar coasters. Goliath remains closed for safety reviews, with eight rides at other parks temporarily shut down. Investigators found Ibn Kariem was ejected from the ride, struck other patrons, and fell beneath the attraction. The Goliath, a 200-foot-tall ride with a 70 mph top speed, used lap bars for restraint. Georgia's Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner's office is conducting an in-depth review of the ride's safety compliance. The incident follows Six Flags Magic Mountain's decision to permanently close its X2 coaster amid lawsuits over alleged brain injuries.

item.title: Dads Take Paid Family Leave as Much as Moms in Key States
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: News Original headline: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are
More fathers are taking paid family leave for new babies, sometimes matching or exceeding the time mothers take. In California, men accounted for 51% of bonding leave claims in 2025, up from 18% in 2004. Similar trends occurred in Colorado and Washington, where men surpassed women for the first time. Karlo Campana, a father of three, took paid leave after each child’s birth, emphasizing the importance of family support. California’s program offers up to eight weeks of paid bonding leave, alongside disability leave for mothers. Molly Weston Williamson of Paid Leave for All noted shifting gender norms and higher benefits—now up to 90% of income—encouraging more dads to participate. Economic pressures, including rising child-rearing costs, also drive demand for paid leave. Federal efforts to boost birth rates and affordability concerns highlight the issue. Despite progress, data gaps remain, as the state program only tracks those who use it. Pew Research found 84% of parents find paid leave helpful, though only half have access. The trend reflects broader cultural shifts toward shared caregiving responsibilities.

item.title: PROFILE: Susan Ann Hume Dies at 81
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Susan Ann Hume
Susan Ann Hume, 81, died Tuesday, October 20, after a short illness. Born June 14, 1945, in Long Beach, CA, she grew up in Downey, CA. She earned a bachelor’s degree in early education from San Jose State and taught grade school in San Diego for over 30 years, obtaining a master’s degree. She married Joe Hume in 1969, and they had son Travis in 1974. The couple moved to Sherwood, Oregon, in 2010 to be closer to Travis and his wife, Rory. Sue became a grandmother in 2012 with the birth of her grandson Harrison, whom she cherished. Survived by Travis, Rory, Harrison, and sister Deborah Menegay Robson, an open house in her memory will be held Sunday, November 8, at Travis and Rory’s home. Details available by email.

item.title: CEO Near Launch of Psilocybin Pill After Years of Trials
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: After a long, strange trip, this CEO is close to taking a psilocybin pill to market
Kabir Nath, former pharmaceutical executive, leads Compass Pathways in developing a psilocybin pill for treatment-resistant depression. After leaving his job in 2022, Nath joined the startup, which is nearing FDA approval for its drug COMP360. Compass has expanded its team, marketing, and office space in Jersey City, with plans for a public rollout if approved. The company's trials show nearly half of participants experienced a 50% reduction in depressive symptoms within six weeks. FDA approval remains uncertain, with potential risks of investor panic and bankruptcy if denied. Nath emphasizes the drug's therapeutic potential for 4 million patients unresponsive to traditional antidepressants. Compass faces competition from other psychedelic firms like AtaiBeckley, which also seeks FDA approval. Nath notes the drug's administration involves a controlled, non-psychotherapeutic process in a quiet room with music. The company is preparing sales teams and clinician partnerships for potential market entry as early as 2024.

item.title: PROFILE: John Demos, 95, Dies at Home; Remembered for Red Fox Steakhouse and Family
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: John Demos
John Demos died at 95 in his home on September 7, 2026. A private service was held September 17. He operated the Red Fox Steakhouse in San Diego from 1966 until its closure in 2025. Born in Chicago during the Great Depression, Demos worked at 10 with his brother Spiro at their father’s cafeteria. The family moved to San Diego in 1946, where he graduated from high school in 1948. He served in the U.S. Coast Guard during the Korean War as a sonar radar man. In 1960, Demos and Spiro opened the Demos Coffee Shop, where he met his wife Rosemarie. They had three sons, including predeceased Billy, and four grandchildren. Demos enjoyed handball, golf, poker, and travel, and was proud of his Greek heritage. He wished donations to ARC of San Diego for disabled programs. Predeceased by parents, brother, and son, he is survived by nieces and extended family.

item.title: PROFILE: John Joseph Standley Dies at 75
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: John Joseph Standley
John Joseph Standley died from metastatic pancreatic cancer on October 13, 2026, in Coronado, California. Born on July 10, 1951, in Denver, Colorado, he was the son of John Stewart Standley and Mary Helen Standley. After attending East High School and graduating from the University of Colorado, Boulder, he worked in construction to fund law school. Standley moved to San Diego after visiting a college friend, Doug Kipperman, and met Carolyn Slack while studying law at Western State University. They married in 1981 and lived in Coronado. He practiced law, later focusing on professional liability claims, and spent 23 years with Richard Kipperman and Corporate Management, Inc. He earned an MBA through San Diego State University. Survived by his wife Carolyn, daughters Katherine Root and Elizabeth Standley, and grandchildren, Standley’s family noted his devotion to family and faith. His cremated remains will be buried at El Camino Memorial Cemetery. A memorial mass will be held at Sacred Heart Catholic Church on November 13.
